title: Approval invalidation - material evidence changes after approval; re-approval on the new bundle
scenarioRefNote: Maps to scenarios.yaml `approval-invalidation`, which explicitly defers the post-invalidation disposition ('re-approval vs block is fixed by the golden cases under human signoff, not invented here'). THIS case fixes that answer, subject to captain signoff: re-evaluate on the new bundle; if still proceed, the SAME stages re-run against the new decision hash. Beyond the prompt-2 twelve (demo-contract §5 branch).

signoff.note: Expected outcomes are product truth subject to captain signoff. DECISION DRAFTED HERE (flagged for the captain): after ApprovalInvalidated, the request re-evaluates on the refreshed bundle; a still-proceed result re-runs the SAME approval stages bound to the NEW decision hash (prior approvals never carry over); a no-longer-proceed result becomes the blocked/prohibited decision the new facts dictate.

trigger.description: Advisor enters the $75,000 request; both approvals land. Before execution, a new pending distribution (15000 USD) posts against the household, changing the liquidity basis the approvals were bound to.
trigger.maskedRequestSummary: distribute 75000 USD; material evidence changes between approval and execution (tokenized)

householdEvidence.summary: No pending activity at first evaluation. AFTER approval, a 15000 USD pending distribution posts - pre-execution revalidation observes it (effective liquidity 285000; reserve still satisfied: 285000 - 75000 = 210000 >= 48000).
Six-month reserve = 48000 USD; satisfied on BOTH the original and the refreshed basis - the invalidation fires on material change, not on breach.

householdInstructions.summary: Taxable source preferred; unchanged by the new pending activity.

expectedAuthority.note: The stage runs TWICE end to end: once against the original decision hash, and - after invalidation - again in full against the derived decision's new hash. Approvals bind to a hash, never to a request.

expectedExecutionEligibility.reason: Eligibility is reached only AFTER the second, re-approved pass: revalidation detected the changed bundle, invalidated the first approvals, and the re-run stages cleared against the new hash.

expectedExplanationNodes.summary: Pre-execution revalidation rebuilt the evidence basis and found a new 15000 USD pending distribution - the input-bundle hash changed, so the approvals no longer describe what would execute.
Approvals are bound to the exact decision hash (v3 invariant 19); a changed bundle invalidates them automatically - facts changed, so consent must be given again, visibly.
Re-evaluation on the refreshed bundle still proceeds (reserve satisfied at 210000 vs 48000), so the same dual-approval stage re-runs against the derived decision - prior approvals never carry over.

expectedLedgerEvents.note: Original evaluation snapshots pinned (no pending activity).
Original proceed decision with dual-approval authority.
First operations approver approves against the original hash.
Second, distinct operations approver approves; quorum satisfied.
Revalidation snapshot records the NEW 15000 USD pending distribution.
Both approvals invalidated: reason material-evidence-changed, carrying the prior decision hash and the new bundle hash.
Derived proceed decision (derivedFromDecisionId = the original) on the new bundle, requiring the same stage afresh.
Re-approval one against the NEW hash.
Re-approval two, distinct actor; quorum satisfied on the new hash.
Reservation created for the re-approved decision.
Single external instruction started under the derived decision's idempotency key.

expectedVerificationState.note: The demo's approval-invalidation moment (demo-contract §3, 3:20-4:05): the timeline shows approval, the detected change, the invalidation, and the re-approval as distinct recorded facts. Execution/status carry fake-adapter-response provenance until the sandbox trigger fires.
